title: Huawei scientist says Nvidia will soon hit the same chip wall
excerpt: A top Huawei scientist warns Nvidia will soon face a physical limit on chip performance, the ceiling Huawei says is reshaping the whole industry.
content_html:
One of the Chinese company’s top scientists has warned that Nvidia will soon run into the same physical limit on chip performance that Huawei says is reshaping the whole industry, according to Bloomberg.

The argument is less a boast than a bet on where the technology is heading. If every chipmaker is nearing a hard ceiling on how much faster silicon can get, then Nvidia’s commanding lead becomes less durable than its share price assumes.

The claim builds on Huawei’s own reframing of progress. Its chip chief He Tingbo, sometimes called the company’s ‘chip queen’, unveiled a Tau Scaling Law that measures advances by how fast signals travel across a circuit rather than by shrinking transistors.

The point of that reframing is survival under sanctions. Cut off from the most advanced lithography, Huawei has an interest in arguing that the old road, ever-smaller transistors, is running out for everyone, not only for the companies barred from the best tools.

Its answer is to build upward. A design Huawei calls LogicFolding stacks circuitry into vertical layers, which it says lifts transistor density sharply and reaches advanced-node performance without the equipment it cannot buy.

The hurdles are real. Stacking chips this way concentrates heat, strains design software, and raises hard questions about manufacturing yield, none of which Huawei has shown it has solved at scale.

Nvidia is not conceding the premise. Jensen Huang has called the folding approach a breakthrough while insisting it is no threat, and he has warned that a Chinese champion running on Huawei chips would be a ‘horrible outcome’ for American technology.

The warning lands in a market bent by policy. US export controls have pushed China’s chip industry away from Nvidia’s GPUs and toward custom ASICs and homegrown parts, accelerating exactly the divergence Huawei is describing.

For now, the distance is still wide. American assessments put Nvidia years and several multiples of performance ahead of Huawei, a lead the physical-limit argument is meant to erode over time rather than overnight.

There is a narrower version of the same claim. Gains in AI chips increasingly hinge on memory bandwidth as much as raw compute, and Huawei has been racing to build its own high-bandwidth memory to close that specific gap.

The messaging is deliberate. Beijing recently put Huawei’s secret chip lab on national television, and its executives have leaned into the narrative that Chinese engineering can route around American controls.

The stakes are enormous for both sides. China is one of Nvidia’s largest potential markets, and Huang has said his company has largely conceded it to Huawei under the weight of export controls.

Huawei’s claims deserve scrutiny as much as attention. The company has every incentive to talk up a future in which its constraints become everyone’s, and its boldest projections run to 2031, far enough out to be hard to test today.

Whether the wall arrives on Huawei’s schedule is the open question. If Nvidia keeps finding performance through packaging, software, and memory, the ceiling Huawei is counting on could stay comfortably out of reach.

The timing is not accidental, either. Framing a shared limit is a way to reset expectations while Huawei is behind, turning a gap it cannot yet close into a race it says nobody can keep winning.

The dispute is ultimately about who writes the next chapter of computing. If the gains from shrinking transistors really are running out, the advantage shifts to whoever designs most cleverly around the limit.

The warning is, in the end, a wager on time. Huawei is betting that physics eventually flattens the field, and that when it does, the company that spent the sanctions years building an alternative path will be the one still climbing.

content_html_zh:
据彭博社报道，这家中国公司的一位顶尖科学家警告说，英伟达很快就会遇到与华为所说的正在重塑整个行业的芯片性能相同的物理极限。

这一论点与其说是吹嘘，不如说是对技术发展方向的押注。 如果每个芯片制造商都接近芯片速度的硬性上限，那么英伟达的领先地位将变得不像其股价所假设的那样持久。

这一说法建立在华为自己对进展的重新构建之上。 其芯片负责人何庭波（有时被称为该公司的“芯片女王”）公布了 Tau 缩放定律，该定律通过信号在电路中传输的速度而不是缩小晶体管来衡量进步。

这种重构的重点是在制裁下生存。 由于与最先进的光刻技术隔绝，华为有兴趣辩称，旧的道路，越来越小的晶体管，对每个人来说都已经耗尽，而不仅仅是对那些被禁止使用最好工具的公司而言。

它的答案是向上构建。 华为称之为 LogicFolding 的设计将电路堆叠到垂直层中，据称这种设计可大幅提升晶体管密度，并在无需使用其无法购买的设备的情况下达到先进节点性能。

障碍是真实存在的。 以这种方式堆叠芯片会集中热量，给设计软件带来压力，并引发有关制造良率的难题，而华为尚未证明其已大规模解决这些问题。

英伟达并没有承认这个前提。 黄仁勋称折叠方法是一次突破，但坚称这不是威胁，他警告说，使用华为芯片运行的中国冠军对于美国技术来说将是一个“可怕的结果”。

这一警告针对的是受政策影响的市场。 美国的出口管制已将中国芯片行业从英伟达的 GPU 转向定制 ASIC 和国产零部件，这恰恰加速了华为所描述的分歧。

目前看来，距离还很遥远。 美国的评估显示，英伟达的性能领先华为数年甚至数倍，这一领先地位的物理限制争论意味着随着时间的推移而不是一夜之间就会被削弱。

同一主张还有一个更窄的版本。 人工智能芯片的收益越来越取决于内存带宽和原始计算，华为一直在竞相构建自己的高带宽内存，以缩小这一特定差距。

消息传递是故意的。 北京最近将华为的秘密芯片实验室放在国家电视台上，其高管倾向于认为中国的工程技术可以绕过美国的控制。

对于双方来说，赌注都是巨大的。 中国是英伟达最大的潜在市场之一，黄仁勋表示，在出口管制的压力下，该公司在很大程度上将其让给了华为。

华为的说法值得仔细审查和关注。 该公司有充分的动机去谈论一个未来，在这个未来中，它的限制将成为每个人的限制，并且其最大胆的预测持续到 2031 年，这个时间已经足够长，以至于今天很难进行测试。

隔离墙是否按照华为的时间表到达还是一个悬而未决的问题。 如果英伟达继续通过封装、软件和内存来寻找性能，那么华为所指望的上限可能会遥不可及。

这个时机也并非偶然。 制定共同限制是在华为落后时重新设定期望的一种方式，将其尚未缩小的差距转变为一场据称没有人能够继续获胜的竞赛。

争论的最终焦点在于谁将书写计算的下一个篇章。 如果缩小晶体管带来的收益真的耗尽，那么优势就会转移到在极限周围设计得最巧妙的人身上。

说到底，这个警告是对时间的赌注。 华为押注物理学最终会使这个领域变得平坦，而当它实现时，这家在制裁期间开辟替代道路的公司将成为仍在攀登的公司。
